Works Great BUT READ ABOUT PARTS - OK - so I have a GE "Quietpower 3" or something like that dishwasher. My wife and kids refuse to get all of the stuck on food off of the dishes before loading the dishwasher. This causes the food to become mixed with the water, and get pumped through the pump and back through the spray arms. Things like Rice and Stickers off of new cups and you name it clog up the arms, EXPECIALLY this center arm. My dishwasher has a lower spinning arm on the bottom of the tub, this one attaches to the underside of the top rack, and then there is the top arm at the top of the dishwasher which is pretty useless. I have taken the arms off at least 50 times and cleaned them by hand in the tub, soaking in vinegar, using pipe cleaners and wire to clear them out. I finally gave up when something got caught inside that I couldn't dislodge. THIS WORKED LIKE A CHARM. However, here is something IMPORTANT FOR ALL TO READ. When you take off the arm under the top rack - KEEP THE SCREW AND WASHER THAT COME OUT. This arm does not have a new replacement screw or washer, and you'll need that to reinstall new arm. This is not a defect or anything - It is just good information to have before you throw out the screw and washer and then have to go digging through the garbage to find it again, clean it and be able to put the new arm on. Also - the part number from GE and the part number for this arm (and pretty much all other arms for dishwashers) do not match. I simply eyeballed the picture and it looked identical and took a chance. It is identical. Works great. Wife is happy. I'll probably end up buying another to pre-plan for the next clog that occurs when my family decides to put a bowl full of rice into the dishwasher without rinsing it out first.

Compact, efficient, well-made! Excellent purchase! - The Giantex mini washing machine is everything I had hoped it would be, and more. This is truly a really mini washing machine with most of the features of a large basic washer. The control panel is simple to use. The load capacity is surprisingly large (one set of twin sheets, or two large bath towels and several wash cloths, or about 7-8 shirts and 4-5 pairs of shorts, or 2-3 pairs of jeans for example). The wash and spin cycles are quick and fairly quiet. The clothes come out clean and spun to a good damp dry. The machine is so light (less than 30 lbs), which makes moving it easy if needed. I bought it to use in a small house we are renting, and it has not disappointed me a bit. It plugs into a standard three-prong grounded outlet and seems to be very energy efficient.
TIPS:
- You will need to purchase a Y-adaptor for the inlet hoses (which I purchased for about $13 at a home improvement store). You cannot select hot, warm, or cold on the machine, so you’ll want to keep your inlet spigots accessible and turn the water on accordingly. I turn them off at the spigot after I’m done washing for the day.
- The water will drain automatically. Our house already had a drain pipe, so we put our outlet hose down in the tube. It has never leaked. The first time I ran it, I did not realize it would drain automatically, just like a full-size washer; so make sure you have it set to drain outside, or into a bucket or sink if needed.
- There is no compartment for adding detergent, so you’ll want to toss in your detergent, fabric softener, bleach, and laundry boosters as the machine fills. I use 1/3 of the detergent I would for a regular machine.

Keep an eye on the filter! - I got one of these for my basement, because it gets really hot and since my game room doubles as my office, it can become sweltering. But if you live in an area of moisture (like a basement, or anywhere on the East Coast), be aware these cooling systems have some limitations.

Here's how it works: you put water in it. It blows air over the water, which is hopefully cold water. It's like continually misting yourself with ice water. That's it, the end. That's the secret to how all these devices work. They're just variants of the same technology.

One innovation with this tool is it shows you how cool it is, which is great (but not necessary, you'll know if it's not working). It also has a filter (curtain) that you wet and put in the freezer, which definitely helps keep things cooler than if you're using water alone. You can even put ice cubes into the receptacle on top.

Center the cap over the pad and using just your fingers lightly cramp on the cap then use your fingernail to press the camp into where the outer rim and the flat surface encircling the coffee and then use your fingers to fold the cap around the outer edges.\It's simple once you get used to it.

Works well enough but doesn't really stay put. - If you're searching for this, you know what it is. My gas range is the standard 36" range with built-in oven that is found in many homes. Nothing fancy. The problem is that there is a small gap between the range and the cabinet/countertop that food or liquid can fall into.

These Stainless Steel Stove Gap Covers solves exactly this problem. Due to its proximity to the fire and heat, the gap cover must be metal and because will be exposed to oils and other food particles, it needs to be easy-to-clean. These covers fit both criteria.

With an extendable piece, these covers can fit all ranges regardless of the depth of the stove and there is a small metal piece that is supposed to provide tension when inserted into the gap. Unfortunately, this is where I have the first problem with this product. The tension just isn't enough to keep the gap cover in the gap snugly. I think a cork or silicone piece would help give it the friction in needs to stay in place.

The second problem I have is that the product is in the shape of the letter "T" but because there is a slight difference in height between my range and the counter, it has to tilt to one side, further making it hard for the cover to stay in place.

The last issue is the extension part. It doesn't lock into a position. Without it, you can accidentally push on the cover and shorten it. It would be better to have some sort of locking mechanism that will keep it to the length that you set.

This product does what its intended for, but I think a few tweaks and it would be perfect (I might just look to see if I can make these tweaks myself).
